newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end mixed, little changed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end mixed, little changed.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures recovered from an afternoon selloff and finished light trading mixed and little changed.
Traders said locals dominated afternoon price swings, with the dearth of outside participation exaggerating moves.
"It was a terrible market," said one floor broker. "We rallied a buck in the last minute.... It was locals all over."
He said the market's erratic moves and thin volume made filling customer orders particularly difficult and vexing.
"It was all locals, no size," agreed another broker of afternoon break down to day's low. "There's nothing going on."

Gains in U.S. Treasury bond futures and the dollar, which rallied sharply again and briefly topped 116.00 yen, helped underpin stock index futures against losses in over-the-counter and high-technology issues.
After the morning rally to the day's peak at 766.10 left resistance intact at 766.40, March S&P 500s pulled back.
The contract tried once again to rise but stalled and formed a double-top on the five-minute bar chart at 765.50, prompting locals to bail out of longs, brokers said.
The turn lower after T-bond futures closed pierced support near 761.90 but respected further support at 760.80.

U.S. economic data Friday morning featured a 1.6 percent drop in November U.S. durable goods orders against forecasts for a 0.1 percent increase, figures which helped support U.S. bond and stock prices.
Some S&P technicians still looked for March S&Ps to challenge their contract high early next week.
March Nikkei index futures drew some moderate-sized firm buying when it was above 19,470.00 in light turnover.
March S&Ps ended flat at 764.60, Value Line rose 1.30 to 691.50, Midcap up 0.20 at 257.50, Russell up 1.65 at 365.40, Nasdaq lost 7.50 to 846.50, Nikkei rose 115.0 to 19,445.0.
